items.title: Los Angeles → Seoul
items.detail:
ALREADY IN LOS ANGELES — nothing to book. You've been in California since the 22nd on the Trybal SoCal trip, tracked separately. No positioning flight to buy; just get yourself to the international terminal.

KE 012 departs LAX 23:50. Korean Air, economy, one checked bag, booking FAFD77. Overnight, arriving Incheon 04:40 on the 29th — the 28th disappears into the date line.

items.title: Seoul → Xi'an, then the city wall
items.detail:
LANDING — KE 141, 09:10 ICN → 11:30 XIY Terminal 5. Four and a half hours on the ground at Incheon before it. Budget an hour for immigration and bags; China takes fingerprints on arrival.

DON'T BUY A CHINESE SIM AT THE AIRPORT. That was the right answer in 2017 and it is the wrong one now: a local SIM sits inside the firewall, which would kill WhatsApp — and WhatsApp is the only channel James actually uses. The travel eSIM you installed at home routes through a foreign carrier, so messaging, mail and maps simply work. A local SIM is worth considering only for the Tibet leg, for rural coverage, and only if the guide arranges it.

TO THE HOTEL — all international flights use T5, and T5 has its own metro station on Line 14. Take it to Xi'an North (about half an hour, ¥7–8), then Line 4 straight down to Dayanta, which puts you at the hotel door. One change, no walking transfer. The fare comes off the ride code inside Alipay; there is no separate transit app in either city. The nonstop airport coach to the Bell Tower leaves from exit 512 on T5's first floor, ¥25, 70–90 minutes — the metro wins.

AFTERNOON — drop bags, then the city wall bike ride. Sandra's Xi'an standout, and the right thing to do on a jet-lagged first afternoon because it asks nothing of you but pedalling. ¥45 for three hours, then ¥5 per extra ten minutes; the deposit is ¥100 in older sources and ¥200 in newer ones, so have ¥200 free. Six rental stations, 13.7 km around, two to three hours for the loop. Return to any station until 20:00; after that everything goes back to South Gate, which stays open until 22:00 with evening returns due by 21:30. Check both brakes before you ride off — Sandra's had one.

EVENING — Muslim Quarter after dark. The other easy win, and a short walk from the wall's north side.

WATER: bottled for everything here, including brushing your teeth, and no ice. Sandra was rigorous about exactly that until she trusted a hostel water cooler in this city, and it cost her the better part of five days — the Terracotta Warriors among them. In 2026 the same five days would cost you the permit handoff, the Z165 and the tour.

items.title: Terracotta Warriors — and it must be today
items.detail:
ALL DAY — the Terracotta Warriors, and it has to be today. Tomorrow is day one of Golden Week and it is the single worst week of the Chinese year to be at a famous monument.

GETTING THERE — from Dayanta it is Line 3 to Tonghuamen, Line 1 to Fangzhicheng, Line 9 to Huaqingchi, exit C, then bus 613 or 602 for the last few minutes. Two changes, about ¥9 all in, and nearer two hours than the ninety minutes it looks on the map — Fangzhicheng is on Lines 1, 6 and 9, not on Line 3 or 4, so the transfer has to happen at Tonghuamen first. Tickets ¥120, and the museum runs 08:30 to 17:00, not into the evening. This is a morning start.

RESERVE AHEAD, AND IN THE RIGHT PLACE — the window is 7 days including the day you book, so 30 September opens on the 24th. Though for holidays the museum has lately released the whole block at once about a week out, so watch for a National Day notice from around the 20th. Book at bmy.com.cn or through the museum's own WeChat account: both take a passport directly, and the gate scanners read it. Not through an OTA — the museum stated in June that it has never authorised a third-party platform. The on-site ticket windows are gone entirely; passport holders now collect at the general service counter rather than buying there, so turning up without a booking is not a plan.

ON THE GROUND — three pits, still being excavated, nothing air-conditioned, which matters far less in October than it did in Sandra's July. One live caveat: Pit 2 has been half-closed for works since 5 September under a notice running about a month, so check whether the south side has reopened before you set out.

EVENING — back by Line 9/4. If there's anything left in you, the Big Wild Goose Pagoda north square fountain show is a five-minute walk from the Westin.

items.title: Golden Week day one — a slow local day
items.detail:
CROWD DAY — do not put anything ticketed or famous here. The 2026 National Day holiday runs 1–7 October, seven consecutive rest days. Your 29th and 30th were ordinary working days; the 1st is day one of the stampede. The right move is a slow local day near the hotel.

SHAANXI HISTORY MUSEUM — a 15-minute walk from the Westin and free. The queue that defeated Sandra twice in 2017 no longer exists, because walking up is not a thing you can do at all now. It is free but ticketed, released 5 days ahead at 17:00 sharp against a daily quota, so the only question is whether you win the release. Book at sxhm.com, the WeChat mini-programme, or the WeChat account (陕西历史博物馆); the website route is the newer one and the easiest with a passport, and prefilling your details is not the same as submitting. Your slot is 26 September at 17:00 China time — 05:00 in Atlanta.

Two things in your favour: through 14 November the museum is running extended hours, 08:30 to 19:00 with last entry at 18:00 and no weekly closing day at all, so a failed morning booking can be retried for an evening slot. If it still fails, the Small Wild Goose Pagoda and the Xi'an Museum nearby are free, quiet and never sell out. The separate Tang murals hall is a paid ticket (¥270) and a different booking; skip it unless you especially want it.

HOUSEKEEPING — confirm the Tibet permit has physically arrived. Repack for a 30-hour train: power bank, earplugs, eye mask, bottled water, cup noodles, and something to eat that isn't cup noodles. Assume no reliable power on a Z-service. The power bank has to be one you bought in Xi'an, not one you flew in — China requires a moulded 3C mark that no US-market battery carries, and lithium can't go in the hold either, so an uncertified one is confiscated at Lhasa on the way to Shanghai.

items.title: Z165 onto the plateau
items.detail:
LEAVE BY 08:00 for a 09:27 departure. Checkout is noon, so the train is no constraint — you'll be gone before breakfast ends.

THE RIGHT STATION — Xi'an Railway Station, 西安站, No. 44 Huancheng North Road, just outside the northeast corner of the wall. NOT Xi'an North (西安北站), which is the high-speed station and the wrong one. From the Westin it is a single Line 4 ride from Dayanta, no changes — which was the whole argument for this hotel.

AT THE STATION — airport-style security, sometimes twice, and water gets scanned with a special reader. Doors open around 20 minutes before departure and the scrum is for luggage space, so be early. No paper ticket: you board on the passport, and a photo or the number alone will not do.

THE TRAIN — Z165 originates in Shanghai and runs Xi'an 09:27 → Lhasa 15:36 the following afternoon. Soft sleeper, four bunks behind a door that closes. Expect other passengers to treat your lower berth as the room's sofa during the day. Thirty hours up the Qinghai–Tibet railway; carriages run oxygen-enriched above Golmud.

Off-grid from here until the 10th.

items.title: Lhasa → Shanghai
items.detail:
Tour ends with the shared transfer to Lhasa Gonggar airport. MU 2336, 15:30 LXA → 21:50 SHA via Xi’an, confirmation GBDPCB, 30,000 Delta miles + ¥170. Kamana flies Lhasa 13:20 to Seoul on Air China (PZC6M0), Jeff probably with her — you are solo from here.

ARRIVAL NIGHT: you land at HONGQIAO, and you fly home from PUDONG. Bags by about 22:20. The Disney side needs a change at Jiangsu Road onto Line 11, whose last train is around 22:30–23:00 — you will not make it, so that leg is a ¥180–250 Didi, 50 km, 60–70 minutes. Downtown is the other option and it is 20 km instead of 50: Line 2 or 10 straight from Hongqiao, or a much shorter taxi. See Stays for whether to split the five nights.

items.title: Lhasa → Shanghai
items.detail:
Tour ends with the shared transfer to Lhasa Gonggar airport. MU 2336, 15:30 → 21:50, changing planes at Xi'an, landing at Hongqiao. Kamana flies Lhasa 13:20 → Seoul on Air China (PZC6M0), Jeff possibly alongside her. You're solo from here.

ONE TAXI YOU CAN'T AVOID — landing at 21:50 means clearing bags around 22:20, and the trip to the Disney area needs a change at Jiangsu Road with the last Line 11 train around 22:30–23:00. You will not make it. Budget a Didi or taxi: roughly 50 km, 60–70 minutes, ¥180–250. One-off, first night only, and still cheaper than five nights of the downtown price difference.

A small gift: Saturday 10 October is a designated national make-up workday, so the country is at work the day you land.

items.title: Shanghai city day
items.detail:
THE CITY DAY, and the right day for it: the park is at its weekend fullest and the museums are open. Line 11 to Jiangsu Road then Line 2 in, or start at the door if you slept downtown.

BOOK FIRST, OR IT DOESN'T HAPPEN. The Urban Planning Exhibition Center at People's Square is free but timed, booked through its WeChat mini-programme, 09:00–17:00 with last entry 16:00, shut Wednesdays. Its window opens SEVEN DAYS OUT, which for Sunday the 11th means 4 OCTOBER — and on the 4th you are somewhere between Shigatse and base camp. Grab it from Lhasa if you have signal; otherwise book the moment you land on Saturday night and accept a Sunday slot may be gone. Top of Sandra's ranking and worth the effort.

A shape that works, roughly north to south:
09:00 Urban Planning Exhibition Center, People's Square. An hour and a half, and the 1:500 city model is the thing.
11:00 Propaganda Poster Art Centre, 7th floor, 726 Yan'an West Road, ¥25, 10:00–17:00. Nine minutes' walk from Jiangsu Road, which is on your own Line 11, so it is easy either side of the park run. Still barely signposted. Sandra's number two.
13:00 Lunch, then the Bund on foot for the Art Deco — the waterfront row is the point, not a museum.
15:30 Yu Gardens and the bird-and-cricket market if there is daylight left. WATCH THE TEA SCAM HERE: the tell is a friendly stranger asking you to take a photo OF THEM. Locals who approach Westerners want to be IN the picture. If the conversation turns to tea, walk away mid-sentence. Sandra fell for this exact one.
Evening: jazz on the Bund. The Fairmont Peace Hotel's bar has run an old-timers' jazz band for decades and you do not need to be a guest.

SKIP the Shanghai Railway Museum — Sandra's one clear dud. And do not shuffle the city onto a Wednesday: the Urban Planning Center is the rare Chinese museum that closes Wednesdays rather than Mondays.

IF YOU WANT LESS WALKING: drop Yu Gardens, and put the Power Station of Art or Tianzifang in instead — both are a short hop and neither needs a timed booking, though check hours in the app on the day.

SUZHOU is now firmly out. Thirty minutes by train and Sandra rated the Silk Museum among the best in China, but it is a 90-minute journey each way from a Disney-side bed and it would eat the one city day you have.

items.title: Shanghai Disneyland, three weekdays
items.detail:
Three full days, all at weekday pricing, on the emptiest days of the autumn. TICKETS: Mon and Tue are covered by the Early Bird 2-Day on Klook (FUW045023, $100.21, confirmed valid both days); Wednesday is a separate ticket and still to buy. GATES 08:30 to 21:30, last entry 20:00, per the booking — a thirteen-hour day if you want it.

ROPE DROP IS THE WHOLE GAME even on a quiet day. First hour: Zootopia: Hot Pursuit, then TRON Lightcycle Power Run — the two that build 60–90 minute lines by mid-morning and hold them. Then Pirates of the Caribbean: Battle for the Sunken Treasure, which is the best thing in the park and not close, and Soaring Over the Horizon. Plan around Peter Pan's Flight rather than dropping into it; this is the version other parks wish they had.

Three days is enough to do the park properly and then re-ride what you liked, so resist buying Premier Access in advance — walk in, read the standby boards, and buy a single ¥140–180 pass only if a wait crosses an hour. Tenth anniversary runs all year as 'With You, It's Magic+': The Heart of Magic on the castle stage, an updated Mickey's Storybook Express, and an anniversary finale on ILLUMINATE!, which closes the park. October also carries the Halloween season.

The metro floods the moment ILLUMINATE ends — either leave straight into it or wait 20–30 minutes. From a Disney-side hotel you just walk, which is most of the argument for staying there.

items.title: Optional park morning, then home
items.detail:
OPTIONAL FOURTH MORNING, and not bought yet: gates 08:30, out by 15:00. It costs a whole 1-Day ticket (¥449–499) because there is no half-day product, so it is only worth it if by Wednesday night you still want more park. Decide on the Wednesday, not now — but if you want the option you have to buy the date in September along with the others.

EITHER WAY: check out, bags at the hotel, and leave for PUDONG — not the Hongqiao you arrived into — by about 15:00. From the Disney side that is a 25-minute taxi; from downtown it is an hour. DL 38 departs 18:25, confirmation JP5E6A, ticket 0062450696002. Then DL 899 LAX 22:50 → ATL 06:07 on the 16th, seat 28A, confirmation G3LX5Q — the return half of the separate SoCal ticket. Seven and a half hours at LAX between them, but they are separate tickets: collect the bag, clear immigration, re-check, possibly change terminals.
